messages.author: c59ab11b418f0190
messages.subject: gl.compliance.check removes longitude data
parts:
Hi there,

I'm using dartR to analyse a non-dart ddRAD dataset - I've imported a vcf file and added all the relevant loc/ind metrics to the appropriate slots to make use of all the dartR functions and it all works well. Except that when I run gl.compliance.check, the longitude data from the gl@other@latlon slot is removed, leaving only the latitude data. 

To understand where maybe I was inputting the data to the slot incorrectly to cause this, I used a dart dataset to look at the standard setup of the gl@other$latlon slot and it looks exactly the same as that of my nondart dataset. And when I run gl.compliance.check on the dart dataset (even though there is no actual need to), it also removes the lon data from the latlon slot and those geographic data no longer work in the functions that require it. 

I can fiddle with my script to work around this and get my longitude data back in there manually but it would be nice to figure out why gl.compliance.check is doing this and use the function as intended. 

My only other thought is that I'm using dartR v2.0.3 and perhaps updating it will solve the issue. I'm always hesitant to update packages and risk having dependency issues so while everything else is working, I prefer not to! 

Any advice would be most appreciated.

Cheers,
Rachel

messages.author: b3d929c6746ca81a
messages.subject: RE: [dartR] gl.compliance.check removes longitude data
parts:
Hi Rachel

 

Within the latlon slot there needs to be a data.frame that has the headers= colnames lat and lon.

 

Does your data have that as it may not recognise it because of missing names.

 

Regards, Bernd

I can fiddle with my script to work around this and get my longitude data back in there manually but it would be nice to figure out why gl.compliance.check is doing this and use the function as intended.

I'm using dartR to analyse a non-dart ddRAD dataset - I've imported a vcf file and added all the relevant loc/ind metrics to the appropriate slots to make use of all the dartR functions and it all works well. Except that when I run gl.compliance.check, the longitude data from the gl@other@latlon slot is removed, leaving only the latitude data. 

To understand where maybe I was inputting the data to the slot incorrectly to cause this, I used a dart dataset to look at the standard setup of the gl@other$latlon slot and it looks exactly the same as that of my nondart dataset.
